context: Current closing price of ON Semiconductor (ON): $69.11 USD as of 2026-11-10.
justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift assumption from what I inferred to be a current price or value near 69–70 units. At the one-day horizon, I anchored closely to the prevailing level, expecting minimal movement and placing the estimate at 69.5, essentially assuming mean reversion dominates over very short windows with only marginal drift. At the one-week horizon, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to 70.0, reflecting a small positive trend assumption while acknowledging that a week is long enough for meaningful directional movement to occur. At the one-month horizon, the estimate rises to 71.0, embodying a continued but modest drift upward — consistent with a scenario where underlying fundamentals are mildly supportive but not dramatically so.

The confidence interval widths reflect the standard reality that uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, the 90% interval spans only 6 units (66.5 to 72.5), reflecting low expected volatility over such a short window and the assumption that large moves within a single session are relatively rare. At one week, the interval widens to 14 units (63 to 77), accounting for the accumulation of daily volatility and the possibility of a trend establishing itself in either direction. At one month, the interval expands dramatically to 28 units (57 to 85), reflecting the full compounding of uncertainty across roughly 20 trading sessions and the genuine possibility of regime shifts, news shocks, or macroeconomic developments altering the trajectory significantly.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside these intervals include sudden macroeconomic announcements such as central bank policy surprises, geopolitical shocks, or unexpected earnings or data releases that could cause gap moves well beyond the one-day interval in a single session. At longer horizons, structural changes in market sentiment, liquidity crises, or correlated asset contagion could send the value meaningfully below 57 or above 85 within the month. The one-month interval in particular, while already wide, does not fully capture tail scenarios involving black swan events or cascading feedback loops.

It is also worth noting that my intervals assume roughly log-normal or normally distributed returns with relatively stable volatility — an assumption that often breaks down in practice. Volatility clustering means that if realized volatility is already elevated at the time of the forecast, my intervals may be systematically too narrow, especially at the one-week and one-month horizons. Conversely, if conditions are unusually calm, the intervals may be conservative. Any significant shift in the underlying volatility regime represents the most underappreciated risk to the reliability of these forecasts.
